summary.headline: KISCO Holdings to absorb Hanguk Steel via share exchange; tender offer gave 78.34% stake, shares issued up to 865,950
summary.what_happened: KISCO Holdings Corp. is carrying out a comprehensive share exchange to make Hanguk Steel Co., Ltd. a wholly-owned subsidiary, with an exchange ratio of 1 : 0.4261670. Following a tender offer at KRW 13,000 per share, KISCO Holdings' stake in Hanguk Steel rose from 60.34% to 78.34%, and the maximum number of new shares to be issued fell from 3,661,911 to 865,950; Hanguk Steel is expected to be delisted after the exchange.

key_numbers.label: KISCO Holdings stake in Hanguk Steel after tender offer
Maximum new KISCO Holdings shares to be issued

summary.why_it_matters: In Korea, share exchanges that make a listed company a wholly-owned subsidiary typically convert the remaining minority shareholders' holdings into shares of the parent company, and the subsidiary's listing is often subsequently removed. Dissenting shareholders generally have a statutory right to demand purchase of their shares at a set price.
